root_cause.text: `iavf_config_rss_reg()` in the iavf driver used `<= adapter->rss_key_size / 4` and `<= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4` as loop bounds, so when iterating over the RSS key/lookup-table dwords it accessed one element past the end of the allocated arrays and wrote past the last valid device register index.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes both loops in `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf_main.c` from `for (i = 0; i <= adapter->rss_key_size / 4; i++)` / `<= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4` to `<`, and the CVE text explicitly states that `rss_{key,lut}_size / 4` is the number of dwords so `<=` causes off-by-one out-of-bounds reads and register writes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one errors in RSS key and LUT register programming loops.
intent_record.what: The loop bounds in iavf_config_rss_reg() were changed from inclusive comparisons to exclusive comparisons: both loops now iterate with `i < adapter->rss_key_size / 4` and `i < adapter->rss_lut_size / 4` instead of `i <= ... / 4`.
intent_record.how: This reduces the number of 32-bit writes by one element in each loop, preventing the code from accessing and programming one word past the intended RSS key and LUT buffers, which could otherwise cause out-of-bounds reads or writing an extra hardware register entry.

candidates.rationale: This loop uses an inclusive upper bound, so it iterates one time too many and reads/writes one dword past the end of the RSS key array/register range.

This inclusive bound causes one extra iteration over the RSS LUT dwords, leading to an out-of-bounds access and register write.
With the off-by-one loop bound, this statement writes the final extra LUT entry beyond the intended array/register limit.
